# pefftacular

> Pure-Python, zero-dependency library for reading and writing PEFF (PSI Extended FASTA
> Format) files: FASTA plus structured per-entry proteomics annotations.

This file is a self-contained usage guide for pefftacular (version 0.4.x). It lists every
public name with its signature, explains the data model, and gives worked examples that
run as written. Source: https://github.com/tacular-omics/pefftacular

## Install

```bash
pip install pefftacular        # or: uv add pefftacular
```

Requires Python 3.12 or newer. No runtime dependencies.

## What PEFF looks like

A PEFF file is FASTA with a structured header and `\Key=value` annotations on each
description line:

```
# PEFF 1.0
# GeneralComment=Example
# //
# DbName=Example DB
# Prefix=sp
# DbVersion=2024_01
# DbSource=https://www.uniprot.org
# NumberOfEntries=1
# SequenceType=AA
# //
>sp:P12345 \PName=Example protein \GName=EXMP \NcbiTaxId=9606 \Length=16 \ModResUnimod=(2|UNIMOD:21|Phospho)
MKTIIALSYIFCLVFA
```

- Line 1 must be `# PEFF <version>` (only 1.0 is fully supported).
- `# //` separates blocks: everything before the first `# //` is file-level
  (`GeneralComment=` lines are kept), then one block per database.
- Entry lines are `>Prefix:UniqueId` followed by space-separated `\Key=value` pairs.
- Multi-item values are parenthesized and concatenated: `(A|B)(C|D)`. Components are
  separated by `|`.
- Escaping (spec §3.3.3): inside items, `\|`, `\(`, `\)`, `\\` are literal characters.
  Balanced parentheses in text (e.g. `N-linked (GlcNAc...)`) are not escaped.

## Public API at a glance

Everything is importable from the package root:

```python
from pefftacular import (
    # I/O
    read_peff, PeffReader, write_peff,
    # header models
    FileHeader, DatabaseHeader, CustomKeyDef, OptionalTagDef,
    # entry model
    SequenceEntry,
    # annotation models
    VariantSimple, VariantComplex, ModResUnimod, ModResPsi, ModRes,
    Processed, DisulfideBond, Proteoform, SequenceRange, CustomKeyValue,
    # errors and warnings
    PeffError, PeffParseError, PeffWriteError, PeffWarning,
)
import pefftacular
pefftacular.__version__   # e.g. "0.4.3"
```

All models are `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`: immutable, compared by value. Use
`dataclasses.replace(obj, field=new)` to derive a modified copy.

## Reading

### read_peff

```
read_peff(source: str | Path | IO[str]) -> tuple[FileHeader, list[SequenceEntry]]
```

Parse an entire PEFF file (path or text-mode stream) into its header and a list of
entries. Opens paths as UTF-8. Logs an INFO summary on `pefftacular.parser`.

```python
from pefftacular import read_peff

header, entries = read_peff("tests/fixtures/PEFF_Tiny_Valid.peff")
print(header.peff_version, [db.prefix for db in header.databases])
for entry in entries:
    print(entry.prefix, entry.db_unique_id, entry.pname, len(entry.sequence))
```

### PeffReader

```
PeffReader(source: str | Path | IO[str])
    .header -> FileHeader          # property; parses the header on first access, cached
    __iter__() -> Iterator[SequenceEntry]
    __enter__() -> Self
    __exit__(exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) -> None   # closes the file if the reader opened it
```

Lazy reader: entries are parsed one at a time, so memory stays flat for large databases.

```python
from pefftacular import PeffReader

with PeffReader("tests/fixtures/PEFF_Tiny_Valid.peff") as reader:
    file_header = reader.header
    for entry in reader:
        print(entry.db_unique_id)
```

Notes:

- A reader iterates **once**. It wraps a single line iterator; a second loop over the
  same reader yields nothing. Create a new reader to read again.
- Use it as a context manager when passing a path, so the file it opened is closed.
  When you pass a stream, the caller owns and closes it.
- The `NumberOfEntries` check (see Warnings) runs when iteration finishes.

### Reading from a string

Any iterable of lines works through a text stream:

```python
import io
from pefftacular import read_peff

text = """# PEFF 1.0
# //
# DbName=Demo
# Prefix=sp
# DbVersion=1
# DbSource=local
# NumberOfEntries=1
# SequenceType=AA
# //
>sp:P1 \\PName=Demo protein \\Length=8 \\VariantSimple=(3|W|dbSNP)
MKTAYIAK
"""
header, entries = read_peff(io.StringIO(text))
entry = entries[0]
print(entry.pname)             # Demo protein
print(entry.length)            # 8
print(entry.variant_simple)    # (VariantSimple(position=3, new_amino_acid='W', tag='dbSNP', annot_id=None),)
```

## Writing

### write_peff

```
write_peff(header: FileHeader, entries: Iterable[SequenceEntry], dest: str | Path | IO[str]) -> None
```

Write a complete PEFF file. `dest` is a path (opened as UTF-8, overwritten) or a
text-mode stream. Entries are validated first: a `None` header, an empty `prefix`, an
empty `db_unique_id` or an empty `sequence` raises `PeffWriteError` before anything is
written. Sequences are wrapped at 60 characters. Annotation keys are written in a fixed
canonical order: `ID`, `DbUniqueId`, `Length`, `PName`, `GName`, `NcbiTaxId`, `TaxName`,
`SV`, `EV`, `PE`, `Decoy`, `Comment`, `VariantSimple`, `VariantComplex`, `ModResUnimod`,
`ModResPsi`, `ModRes`, `Processed`, `DisulfideBond`, `Proteoform`, custom keys, then
`extra` keys. File-system errors (missing directory, permissions) propagate as the usual
`OSError` subclasses, not `PeffWriteError`.

```python
import io
from pefftacular import DatabaseHeader, FileHeader, ModResUnimod, SequenceEntry, write_peff

db = DatabaseHeader(
    prefix="sp",
    db_name="SwissProt",
    db_version="2024_01",
    db_sources=("https://www.uniprot.org",),
    number_of_entries=1,
    sequence_type="AA",
)
header = FileHeader(peff_version="1.0", databases=(db,))
entry = SequenceEntry(
    prefix="sp",
    db_unique_id="P12345",
    sequence="MKTIIALSYIFCLVFA",
    pname="Example protein",
    gname="EXMP",
    mod_res_unimod=(ModResUnimod(positions=(2,), accession="UNIMOD:21", name="Phospho"),),
)

buf = io.StringIO()
write_peff(header, [entry], buf)
print(buf.getvalue())
# write_peff(header, [entry], "output.peff")   # or to a path
```

Output:

```
# PEFF 1.0
# //
# DbName=SwissProt
# Prefix=sp
# DbVersion=2024_01
# DbSource=https://www.uniprot.org
# NumberOfEntries=1
# SequenceType=AA
# //
>sp:P12345 \PName=Example protein \GName=EXMP \ModResUnimod=(2|UNIMOD:21|Phospho)
MKTIIALSYIFCLVFA
```

### Round trip

```python
import io
from pefftacular import read_peff, write_peff

header, entries = read_peff("tests/fixtures/PEFF_AnnotID_Insulin_Valid.peff")
buf = io.StringIO()
write_peff(header, entries, buf)
header2, entries2 = read_peff(io.StringIO(buf.getvalue()))
assert entries2 == entries
```

Round trips preserve the parsed *models*, not the exact text: key order is normalized,
`\OX=` is written back as `\NcbiTaxId=`, and header keys are written in a fixed order.

## Header models

### FileHeader

```
FileHeader(peff_version: str, general_comments: tuple[str, ...] = (), databases: tuple[DatabaseHeader, ...] = ())
```

Top-level header. `peff_version` is the string from the first line (e.g. `"1.0"`).
`general_comments` holds file-level `GeneralComment=` lines (before the first `# //`).
`databases` holds one `DatabaseHeader` per database block.

### DatabaseHeader

```
DatabaseHeader(
    prefix: str | None = None,
    db_name: str | None = None,
    db_description: str | None = None,
    db_version: str | None = None,
    db_date: str | None = None,
    db_sources: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    general_comments: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    number_of_entries: int | None = None,
    sequence_type: str | None = None,
    decoy: bool | None = None,
    conversion: str | None = None,
    has_annotation_identifiers: bool = False,
    proteoform_db: bool = False,
    custom_key_defs: tuple[CustomKeyDef, ...] = (),
    optional_tag_defs: tuple[OptionalTagDef, ...] = (),
    extra: dict[str, str] = {},
)
```

Metadata for one database block. Mapping to header keys:

| field | header key |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | `Prefix` (matches the `>prefix:` of its entries) |
| `db_name` | `DbName` |
| `db_description` | `DbDescription` |
| `db_version` | `DbVersion` |
| `db_date` | `DbDate` |
| `db_sources` | `DbSource` (repeatable) |
| `general_comments` | `GeneralComment` inside the block (repeatable) |
| `number_of_entries` | `NumberOfEntries` (int; a non-integer raises `PeffParseError`) |
| `sequence_type` | `SequenceType` (e.g. `AA`, `NA`) |
| `decoy` | `Decoy` (`true`/`1`/`yes` → True) |
| `conversion` | `Conversion` |
| `has_annotation_identifiers` | `HasAnnotationIdentifiers` (case-insensitive; also `HasAnnotationIdentifier`) |
| `proteoform_db` | `ProteoformDb` (case-insensitive; also `IsProteoformDB`) |
| `custom_key_defs` | `CustomKeyDef` (repeatable) |
| `optional_tag_defs` | `OptionalTagDef` (repeatable, `tag:description`) |
| `extra` | any other `Key=value` line in the block |

`SpecificKey` and `SpecificValue` lines are accepted but discarded. The mandatory keys
`DbName`, `Prefix`, `DbVersion`, `DbSource`, `NumberOfEntries`, `SequenceType` each emit a
`PeffWarning` when missing.

### CustomKeyDef

```
CustomKeyDef(
    key_name: str,
    description: str,
    concept_curie: str | None = None,
    regexp: str | None = None,
    field_names: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    field_types: tuple[str, ...] = (),
)
```

Declares a custom per-entry key, from a header line such as:

```
# CustomKeyDef=(KeyName=Score|Description="A score"|FieldNames=method,value,passed|FieldTypes=string,decimal,boolean)
```

Quoted values (`"..."`) may contain `|`; inside quotes only `\"` and `\\` are escapes, so
regular expressions keep their backslashes. When a database declares a custom key, entry
values for that key are parsed into `CustomKeyValue`s (see below) instead of `extra`.

### OptionalTagDef

```
OptionalTagDef(tag: str, description: str)
```

From `# OptionalTagDef=tag:description`. The tag can then appear as the optional last
component of annotation items (the `tag` fields below).

## Entry model

### SequenceEntry

```
SequenceEntry(
    prefix: str,
    db_unique_id: str,
    sequence: str,
    id: str | None = None,
    db_unique_id_key: str | None = None,
    pname: str | None = None,
    gname: str | None = None,
    ncbi_tax_id: int | None = None,
    tax_name: str | None = None,
    length: int | None = None,
    sv: int | None = None,
    ev: int | None = None,
    pe: int | None = None,
    decoy: bool | None = None,
    comment: str | None = None,
    variant_simple: tuple[VariantSimple, ...] = (),
    variant_complex: tuple[VariantComplex, ...] = (),
    mod_res_unimod: tuple[ModResUnimod, ...] = (),
    mod_res_psi: tuple[ModResPsi, ...] = (),
    mod_res: tuple[ModRes, ...] = (),
    processed: tuple[Processed, ...] = (),
    disulfide_bond: tuple[DisulfideBond, ...] = (),
    proteoform: tuple[Proteoform, ...] = (),
    custom_values: dict[str, tuple[CustomKeyValue, ...]] = {},
    extra: dict[str, str] = {},
)
```

| field | source key | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix`, `db_unique_id` | `>prefix:id` | required |
| `sequence` | sequence lines | joined, whitespace stripped |
| `id` | `\ID=` | |
| `db_unique_id_key` | `\DbUniqueId=` | |
| `pname` | `\PName=` | protein name |
| `gname` | `\GName=` | gene name |
| `ncbi_tax_id` | `\NcbiTaxId=` or `\OX=` | int |
| `tax_name` | `\TaxName=` | |
| `length` | `\Length=` | int; mismatch with `len(sequence)` warns |
| `sv`, `ev`, `pe` | `\SV=`, `\EV=`, `\PE=` | int |
| `decoy` | `\Decoy=` | `true`/`1`/`yes` → True |
| `comment` | `\Comment=` | |
| `variant_simple` | `\VariantSimple=` | |
| `variant_complex` | `\VariantComplex=` | |
| `mod_res_unimod` | `\ModResUnimod=` | |
| `mod_res_psi` | `\ModResPsi=` | |
| `mod_res` | `\ModRes=` | |
| `processed` | `\Processed=` | |
| `disulfide_bond` | `\DisulfideBond=` | |
| `proteoform` | `\Proteoform=` | |
| `custom_values` | keys declared by a `CustomKeyDef` for this prefix | |
| `extra` | any other key | raw string values |

A non-integer value for an int key raises `PeffParseError` with the line number.

## Annotation models

Positions are 1-based and inclusive. A position that is not an integer (e.g. `?` for
unknown) is kept as a `str`, which is why position fields are typed `int | str`.

`annot_id` is the optional annotation identifier used when the database sets
`HasAnnotationIdentifiers=true`: an item written `(12:53|...)` has `annot_id=12` and
position 53. Other annotations reference these IDs (see `DisulfideBond`, `Proteoform`).

`tag` is the optional trailing component (often an `OptionalTagDef` tag or a source such
as `dbSNP`).

### VariantSimple

```
VariantSimple(position: int | str, new_amino_acid: str, tag: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Single residue substitution. Item form: `(position|newAminoAcid[|tag])`, e.g. `(225|C|dbSNP)`.

### VariantComplex

```
VariantComplex(start_pos: int | str, end_pos: int | str, new_sequence: str, tag: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Insertion, deletion or multi-residue substitution. Item form:
`(start|end|newSequence[|tag])`; an empty `newSequence` is a deletion.

### ModResUnimod

```
ModResUnimod(positions: tuple[int | str, ...], accession: str, name: str, tag: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Modification with a UNIMOD accession. Item form: `(pos[,pos...]|accession|name[|tag])`,
e.g. `(100|UNIMOD:21|Phospho)`. Several positions share one item as `12,15,20`.

### ModResPsi

```
ModResPsi(positions: tuple[int | str, ...], accession: str, name: str, tag: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Same shape, PSI-MOD accession, e.g. `(31|MOD:00798|half cystine)`.

### ModRes

```
ModRes(positions: tuple[int | str, ...], accession: str, name: str, tag: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Same shape, any accession (may be empty; `ModResUnimod`/`ModResPsi` warn on an empty
accession, all three warn on an empty name).

### Processed

```
Processed(start_pos: int | str, end_pos: int | str, accession: str, name: str, tag: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Processed molecule (signal peptide, propeptide, mature chain). Item form:
`(start|end|accession|name[|tag])`, e.g. `(1|24|PEFF:0001021|signal peptide)`.

### DisulfideBond

```
DisulfideBond(annot_id_refs: tuple[int | str, ...], description: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

Disulfide bond linking two previously declared `ModResPsi` half-cystine annotations **by
annotation ID**, not by residue position (spec §3.4.2). Item form:
`([annotId:]ref1,ref2[|description])`, e.g. `(81:1,2|between chains)` gives
`annot_id=81, annot_id_refs=(1, 2)`. Because they are IDs, these values are never
range-checked against the sequence.

### SequenceRange

```
SequenceRange(start: int | str, end: int | str)
```

A contiguous 1-based inclusive range, used by `Proteoform`. `"1-110"` → `SequenceRange(1, 110)`;
a value with no `-` gives `start == end`.

### Proteoform

```
Proteoform(proteoform_id: str, ranges: tuple[SequenceRange, ...], annot_id_refs: tuple[int, ...], name: str | None = None, annot_id: int | None = None)
```

A specific proteoform: the sequence ranges it keeps and the annotation IDs (processing
events, modifications) it carries. Item form: `(proteoformId|ranges|annotIdRefs[|name])`,
e.g. `(NX_P01308-1-pf1|1-110||preproinsulin)` or `(pf2|25-54,90-110|81,82,83|insulin)`.
`annotIdRefs` must be integers; anything else raises `PeffParseError`.

### CustomKeyValue

```
CustomKeyValue(key_name: str, fields: dict[str, str | int | float | bool | date | time] = {}, raw: str = '')
```

One parsed value of a header-declared custom key. `fields` maps field names to typed
values, `raw` is the original item text.

How values are parsed, for each parenthesized item (or a single bare value):

1. If the `CustomKeyDef` has a `regexp`, it is `fullmatch`ed against the item. Groups map
   in order onto `field_names` (unnamed extras become `field1`, `field2`, ...). Groups that
   did not participate are omitted. A non-matching item warns and gets empty `fields`.
2. Otherwise the item is split on unescaped `|` and zipped with `field_names`.
3. Each field is coerced by the matching `field_types` entry: `integer` → int, `decimal` →
   float, `boolean` → `true`/`1`/`yes`, `date`/`time` → ISO `datetime.date`/`datetime.time`,
   `string` → str, `enumeration(a|b|c)` → str (warns if not a member). A failed coercion
   warns and keeps the raw string. Missing or unknown types stay str.
4. An invalid `regexp` warns (on every value) and the value is then split on `|` instead.

```python
from pefftacular import read_peff

header, entries = read_peff("tests/fixtures/custom_keys.peff")
entry = entries[0]
ss = entry.custom_values["SecondaryStructure"]
print(ss[0].fields["StartPosition"])   # 10  (int)
print(ss[0].fields["Description"])     # Helix
print(ss[0].raw)                       # 10|20|ncithesaurus:C47937|Helix
```

When writing, a non-empty `raw` is emitted verbatim and `fields` is ignored. To write
values you built or edited, set `raw=""` so the writer serializes `fields` (in
`field_names` order when the database declares the key).

## Worked example: annotation IDs, disulfides and proteoforms

```python
from pefftacular import read_peff

header, entries = read_peff("tests/fixtures/PEFF_AnnotID_Insulin_Valid.peff")
db = header.databases[0]
print(db.has_annotation_identifiers)        # True
insulin = entries[0]

by_id = {m.annot_id: m for m in insulin.mod_res_psi}
for bond in insulin.disulfide_bond:
    a, b = (by_id[i] for i in bond.annot_id_refs)
    print(bond.annot_id, a.positions, b.positions, bond.description)

for pf in insulin.proteoform:
    spans = [(r.start, r.end) for r in pf.ranges]
    print(pf.proteoform_id, spans, pf.annot_id_refs, pf.name)
```

## Worked example: filter and rewrite a database

```python
import dataclasses
import io
from pefftacular import read_peff, write_peff

header, entries = read_peff("tests/fixtures/PEFF_AnnotID_Insulin_Valid.peff")

# keep only UNIMOD/PSI-MOD annotations, drop variants
cleaned = [dataclasses.replace(e, variant_simple=(), variant_complex=()) for e in entries]

# keep NumberOfEntries consistent with what we write
db = dataclasses.replace(header.databases[0], number_of_entries=len(cleaned))
header = dataclasses.replace(header, databases=(db,))

out = io.StringIO()
write_peff(header, cleaned, out)
```

## Worked example: streaming a large file

```python
from collections import Counter
from pefftacular import PeffReader

counts: Counter[str] = Counter()
with PeffReader("tests/fixtures/SmallTestDB-PEFF1.0.peff") as reader:
    for entry in reader:
        for mod in entry.mod_res_psi:
            counts[mod.name] += len(mod.positions)
print(counts.most_common(5))
```

## Errors

```
class PeffError(ValueError)
class PeffParseError(PeffError):
    PeffParseError(message: str, *, line: int | None = None, context: str | None = None, hint: str | None = None)
class PeffWriteError(PeffError):
    PeffWriteError(message: str, *, hint: str | None = None)
```

- `PeffError`: base of every pefftacular exception. Subclasses `ValueError`, so existing
  `except ValueError` code keeps working.
- `PeffParseError`: the input cannot be parsed. Attributes: `.line` (1-based absolute line
  number, when known; also prefixed to the message as `Line N: ...`), `.context` (the
  offending text), `.hint` (how to fix it). `context` and `hint` are also attached as PEP
  678 notes, so they appear in tracebacks without changing `str(err)`.
- `PeffWriteError`: a model cannot be serialized. Attribute `.hint`.

Raised for: empty file, bad first line (must be exactly `# PEFF <major>.<minor>`), a
malformed `>prefix:id` line, non-integer int fields, too few components in an annotation
item (`VariantSimple` < 2, `VariantComplex` < 3, `ModRes*` < 3, `Processed` < 4,
`Proteoform` < 2), non-integer proteoform refs, mismatched parentheses.

```python
import io
from pefftacular import PeffError, PeffParseError, read_peff

bad = "# PEFF 1.0\n# //\n# Prefix=sp\n# //\n>sp:P1 \\Length=abc\nMK\n"
try:
    read_peff(io.StringIO(bad))
except PeffParseError as err:
    print(err.line, err.context, err.hint)   # 5 abc Length must be an integer, e.g. Length=1
except PeffError:
    raise
```

## Warnings

```
class PeffWarning(UserWarning)
```

Parsing is permissive: the data is always returned, and spec `MUST` violations are
reported with `warnings.warn(..., PeffWarning)`:

- PEFF version other than 1.0
- a mandatory database header key is missing
- `NumberOfEntries` differs from the number of entries with that prefix (checked when
  iteration finishes)
- `\Length=` differs from the sequence length
- an annotation position (VariantSimple, VariantComplex, ModRes*, Processed) outside
  `1..len(sequence)`; non-integer positions are not checked
- empty `new_amino_acid`, empty ModRes name, empty ModResUnimod/ModResPsi accession
- custom-key value not matching its `RegExp`, failed type coercion, enumeration mismatch,
  invalid `RegExp`

Strict mode:

```python
import warnings
from pefftacular import PeffWarning, read_peff

with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("error", PeffWarning)
    header, entries = read_peff("tests/fixtures/PEFF_Tiny_Valid.peff")   # raises on any violation
```

The deprecated `\Variant=` key emits a `PeffWarning` and its value is stored in
`extra["Variant"]`.

## Logging

The package attaches a `NullHandler` and never configures logging. Loggers are
`pefftacular.parser` and `pefftacular.writer`: `INFO` for totals (entries read/written),
`DEBUG` for file open, header parse and per-prefix counts.

```python
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)
logging.getLogger("pefftacular").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
```

## Gotchas

- **Free-text values are escaped.** `pname`, `gname`, `tax_name` and `comment` are
  written with spec §3.3.3 escaping and unescaped on read. `extra` values are raw and
  written verbatim; a value containing ` \Key=` reads back as a new key.
- **Last duplicate key wins.** If a description line repeats a key, only the last value
  is kept.
- **`SpecificKey` / `SpecificValue` header lines are dropped** and do not round-trip.
- **Readers iterate once.** Create a new `PeffReader` to read the file again.
- **`CustomKeyValue.raw` takes priority on write**: clear it after editing `fields`.
- **`DisulfideBond.annot_id_refs` are annotation IDs, not positions.**
- Header lines must start with `# ` (hash, space) or be exactly `#`; the first other line
  ends the header.

## Related

- Sibling `fastatacular`: plain FASTA with the same reader/writer API shape.
- Downstream tools: `peff_digest`, `peff_uniprot_fetcher` (tacular-omics).
- Spec: `PEFF_SpecDoc_1.0_FINAL.pdf` in the repository, and https://www.psidev.info/peff
